## Packages + Load Data
```{r setup}
library(MCMCpack)
library(ggplot2)

steam_df <- read.csv("steam_clean_v2.csv")
```

## Data

```{r data}
# cleaning col names --> csv files have been reading it weirdly in r
names(steam_df) <- tolower(names(steam_df))
names(steam_df) <- gsub("\\.", "_", names(steam_df))

# print out col names, just makign sure
colnames(steam_df)

# checking price var
summary(steam_df$price)

# creating price tiers, on the log scale (follows my preprocessing file)
steam_df$price_tier <- cut(
  steam_df$price,
  breaks = c(-Inf, log(0 + 1), log(5 + 1), log(15 + 1), log(30 + 1), Inf),
  labels = c("Free", "Low", "Mid", "High", "Premium"),
  right = TRUE
)

steam_df$price_tier <- as.factor(steam_df$price_tier)

# needed variables 
keep_vars <- c("price_tier", "peak_ccu", "recommendations", "positive", "negative")
keep_vars <- keep_vars[keep_vars %in% names(steam_df)]

steam_df <- steam_df[complete.cases(steam_df[, keep_vars]), ]

# running other summaries, for research paper enhancement: 
# data summary 
table(steam_df$price_tier)
prop.table(table(steam_df$price_tier))


# Train / test split (80/20)
set.seed(123)

n <- nrow(steam_df)
train_index <- sample(1:n, size = round(0.8 * n))

train_df <- steam_df[train_index, ]
test_df  <- steam_df[-train_index, ]

#  Bayesian Multinomial Logistic Regression using MCMC package 
# source: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mcmc/mcmc.pdf
bayes_model <- MCMCmnl(
  price_tier ~ peak_ccu + recommendations + positive + negative +
             metacritic_score + achievements + average_playtime_forever + language_count,
  data = train_df,
  mcmc = 5000,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 5,
  verbose = 0
)

summary(bayes_model)
```

## Multinomial model, predicting on test set, confusion matrix 
```{r}
library(nnet)


# dropping the free tier model beccause we purposely removed this in preprocessing
train_df$price_tier <- droplevels(train_df$price_tier)
test_df$price_tier  <- droplevels(test_df$price_tier)

# multinomial model 
multinom_model <- multinom(
  price_tier ~ peak_ccu + recommendations + positive + negative +
             metacritic_score + achievements + average_playtime_forever + language_count,
  data = train_df,
  trace = FALSE
)
# predicting on test set 
pred_class <- predict(multinom_model, newdata = test_df)

# confusion matrix
conf_mat <- table(
  Predicted = pred_class,
  Actual = test_df$price_tier
)

conf_mat


```

## accuracy  
```{r Accuracy }
accuracy <- mean(pred_class == test_df$price_tier)
accuracy
```

## Class-wise accuracy 
```{r}
prop.table(conf_mat, margin = 2)
```

## Plots 
```{r}
# Plot 1: Confusion matrix 

library(reshape2)

conf_prop <- prop.table(conf_mat, margin = 2)
conf_df <- as.data.frame(conf_prop)

ggplot(conf_df, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Freq, 2))) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Confusion Matrix (Proportions)",
    x = "Predicted",
    y = "Actual"
  )

# Plot 2: Distribution of log-scaled game prices shows that it is skewed towards lower priced games 
ggplot(steam_df, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Log-Scaled Game Prices",
    x = "Log(Price + 1)",
    y = "Count"
  )

# Plot 3: 
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Tier, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs Predicted Distribution (Proportion)",
    x = "Price Tier",
    y = "Proportion"
  )

# Plot 4: Probablity confidence -- how confident we are with model 
pred_probs <- predict(multinom_model, newdata = test_df, type = "probs")

max_prob <- apply(pred_probs, 1, max)

ggplot(data.frame(max_prob), aes(x = max_prob)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Prediction Confidence Distribution",
    x = "Max Predicted Probability",
    y = "Count"
  )
```
